items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to prohibiting
the use of certain food packaging and plastic food service ware
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2603

SPONSOR: KRUEGER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to
prohibiting the use of certain food packaging and plastic food service
ware

 
PURPOSE:

To prohibit the use of food service ware that contains polystyrene foam
by food service providers, including state agencies And municipalities,
and their contractors and lessees, as well as restaurants and retail
food vendors. Polystyrene, is used as a means to package prepared food
that can be "taken out" of food establishments by consumers. This bill
would require food service providers to use alternate products that are
compostable or recyclable.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Article 27 is amended to add a new Title 22 Food Service Waste
Reduction.

27-2201 - Definitions.

27-2203 - Prohibited disposable food service ware. Retail food venders,
agencies and municipalities, agency and municipal facility food provid-
ers, agency and municipal contractors and lessees shall not sell
prepared food in disposable food service ware that contains polystyrene
foam.

27-2205 - Required compostable or recyclable disposable food service
ware. All entities covered under section 27-2203 using any disposable
food service ware shall use a suitable, affordable compostable, home
compostable or recyclable product unless there is no such product avail-
able.

27-2207 - Unique packaging or financial hardship waiver. Any not-for-
profit corporation regardless of income, and any retail food vendor with
a gross income under $500,000 per location that is not part of a chain
may request a unique packaging or financial hardship waiver from the
Department of Environmental Conservation.

71-2730 - Anyone in violation shall receive a warning notice for the
first violation. A person shall be liable for a civil penalty of $250
for the first violation after a warning, $500 for the second violation,
and $1,000 for each subsequent violation in the same calendar year.
Enforcement of provisions will be the responsibility of the Departments
of Environmental Conservation, Agriculture and Markets, and Health, and
the Attorney General. Provisions may also be enforced by a village,
town, city, or county, which are empowered to create local laws, ordi-
nances, or regulations consistent with this title.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Polystyrene foam is a liquid hydrocarbon that is commercially manufac-
tured from petroleum. Each year Americans throw away 25,000,000,000
polystyrene foam cups, which equates to 1,369 tons of polystyrene foam
products every day. A single polystyrene foam cup can take up to 500
years to fully disintegrate. Polystyrene foam, or 'Styrofoam' is an
unsustainable product made from petroleum, a fossil fuel and a non-re-
newable resource. Fossil fuels increase carbon dioxide emissions and
other potent greenhouse gases that exacerbate global warming and cause
climate change.

Polystyrene foam is also very difficult to recycle due to its light
weight and low scrap value. It is generally not accepted in curbside
programs, is seldom able to be reused, and takes up a considerable
amount of space in landfills. Research suggests that landfills are
rapidly filling up and contain as much as 30% of the toxin-leaching,
non-biodegradable polystyrene products. Due to the physical properties
of polystyrene foam, the United States Environmental Protection A-gency
states "that such materials can have serious impacts on human health,
wildlife, and the aquatic environment," because the product breaks down,
can clog waterways, and is mistaken for food by wildlife.

Polystyrene foam manufacturers are the fifth largest producers of toxic
waste in the United States (U.S.). One of the components of polystyrene
foam, styrene, is a known hazardous substance which was added to
theòU.S. Health Department's list of carcinogens in June of 2011. Styr-
ene exposure increases the risk of leukemia and lymphoma and is a neuro-
toxin. Many people do not realize that when they reheat food in a polys-
tyrene foam product using a microwave, toxins are released into their
food.

Polystyrene foam bans can be found in California, Florida, Maine, Mary-
land, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, Oregon, Texas, Washington
and Washington D.C. San Francisco, CA realized a 36% decrease in polys-
tyrene food service ware after a one year ban. Food establishments that
have participated in programs to reduce the use of single-use food
service ware have also saved thousands of dollars per year.

Albany County's Chief Executive Dan McCoy expanded a ban on polystyrene
foam service ware in Albany County in September of 2018.  The ban,
initially enacted in 2014 only for chain food establishments, now
requires county government, agencies and those who do business with
Albany County to do the same. A ban on the use of polystyrene single-use
food and beverage containers in New York City, required under Local Law
142, became effective on January 1, 2019.

This bill would address the environmental impacts of polystyrene foam
service ware across New York State, while allowing for exceptions in
cases of financial hardship or where there is no viable alternative
product.

 
FISCAL IMPACT ON THE STATE:

Undetermined.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2017-18 S5837 Same As A10578 Ortiz - died in committee

2015-16 S2782 Same As A 5762 Kavanagh - died in committee

2013-14 S3444-A Same As A 119-A Kavanagh died in committee
2011-12 S426 Same As A 6231 Kavanagh - committee discharged to rules

2009-10 S747-A Same As A 706-A Kavanagh - died in committee

2007-08 S6402 Same As A 9420

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect one year from the date after it shall have
become law.

summary: Enacts the "food service waste reduction act"; provides for a prohibition on the use of certain disposable food service ware; provides definitions and sanctions.
title: Provides for a prohibition on the use of certain disposable food service ware
